thread.title: Lawmakers urge protection of Medicaid amid budget discussions
thread.title_full: Lawmakers urge protection of Medicaid amid budget discussions

author: Tucson Standard
title: Lawmakers urge protection of Medicaid amid budget discussions
text:
Juan Ciscomani, U.S. Representative for Arizona's 6th Congressional District | Official Website
Juan Ciscomani, U.S. Representative for Arizona's 6th Congressional District | Official Website
U.S. Congressman Juan Ciscomani, along with 15 other lawmakers, has called on Senate and House leaders to safeguard Medicaid. They oppose any legislation that would limit access to Medicaid coverage for vulnerable individuals or compromise hospitals' ability to provide care.
In a letter addressed to Senate Majority Leader John Thune and House Speaker Mike Johnson, the lawmakers emphasized their commitment to ensuring federal spending cuts do not affect their most vulnerable constituents. "Throughout the budget process, we have consistently affirmed our commitment to ensuring that reductions in federal spending do not come at the expense of our most vulnerable constituents," they wrote.
The letter criticized provisions in a proposal released by the Senate Finance Committee on June 16, which exceed those in H.R. 1. The lawmakers urged that the House's approach be retained in the final bill, describing it as more pragmatic and compassionate.
"Protecting Medicaid is essential for the vulnerable constituents we were elected to represent," they stated. "Therefore, we cannot support a final bill that threatens access to coverage or jeopardizes the stability of our hospitals and providers."
Earlier this year, Ciscomani had joined other representatives in opposing any reconciliation package that reduces Medicaid coverage for those with limited health coverage options. He also engaged with various stakeholders to prevent changes detrimental to Arizona's healthcare funding from being included in legislative packages.
Ciscomani was part of a group within the Congressional Hispanic Conference that expressed concerns over potential Medicaid cuts' impact on rural and predominantly Hispanic communities.
The recent letter was penned by Congressman David Valadao (R-CA) and signed by Reps. Rob Bresnahan (R-PA), Chuck Edwards (R-NC), Young Kim (R-CA), Andrew Garbarino (R-NY), Michael Lawler (R-NY), Jen Kiggans (R-VA), Jeff Van Drew (R-NJ), Don Bacon (R-NE), Dan Newhouse (R-WA), Zach Nunn (R-IA), Rob Wittman (R-VA), Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY), Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA), and Jeff Hurd (R-CO).
The letter reiterated support for reforms outlined in H.R. 1 aimed at strengthening Medicaid for children, pregnant women, the elderly, and individuals with disabilities while criticizing aspects of the Senate's proposal related to provider taxes and state-directed payments.
"We appreciate your ongoing leadership in advocating for our members’ priorities as you engage in negotiations with the Senate," concluded the letter.
